subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Cam Motion Laws: Designing the Curve
description: A micro-lesson that makes Cam Motion Laws: Designing the Curve usable.

hook.text: How the follower speeds up and slows down matters as much as how far it goes.

buildup.text: Simple harmonic, cycloidal, and polynomial motions each have trade-offs.

discovery.text: Smooth acceleration profiles reduce shock and vibration at high speed.

twist.text: A parabolic motion law has sudden jerk — it slams the follower at transitions.

climax.text: Modern cams use polynomial curves tuned for minimal vibration and wear.

punchline.text: The curve decides if the cam whispers or screams.

quiz.question: Why do engineers avoid parabolic cam motion at high speed?
options: Parabolic motion is too slow for fast applications
Sudden changes in acceleration create jerk that causes shock and vibration
Parabolic profiles wear the cam surface too quickly
